easy.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah At-Tin
easy.explain: Surah At-Tin opens: "By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai, and this secure city."

easy.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah Ash-Shams
easy.explain: Surah Ash-Shams swears by the sun, the moon, the day, the night, the sky, the earth and the soul.

easy.set: The seven whom Allah will shade on the Day of Judgement
items: One whose heart is attached to the mosque
Two who love each other for Allah
One who refuses a tempting invitation out of fear of Allah
One who gives charity in secret
One who remembers Allah alone and weeps
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ named seven people Allah will shade on the day when there is no shade but His.

easy.set: The five acts of the fitrah
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said five things are of the fitrah: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the moustache, cutting the nails and plucking the armpit hair.

easy.set: The parts of the body that touch the ground in sujud
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (and he pointed to his nose), the two hands, the two knees and the ends of the two feet.

easy.set: The four things a woman may be married for
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said a woman is married for four things and told us to choose the one with religion.

easy.set: The rights of a Muslim over another Muslim
items: Praying for him when he sneezes
Visiting him when he is ill
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ listed six rights: greet him, accept his invitation, advise him, respond when he sneezes and praises Allah, visit him when sick, and follow his funeral.

easy.set: Gates of Paradise named in one hadith of al-Bukhari
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said people of prayer, jihad, fasting and charity will be called from their gates, and the gate of fasting is ar-Rayyan.
The Prophet ﷺ set Dhul-Hulayfah, al-Juhfah, Qarn al-Manazil and Yalamlam. Umar later set Dhat 'Irq for Iraq.

easy.set: The commanders at Mu'tah, in the order they took the banner
easy.explain: Zayd took the banner and fell, then Ja'far, then Ibn Rawahah, and then Khalid, a sword of Allah.
The Qur'an mentions the hoopoe of Sulayman, the raven sent to Adam's son, and the quails sent to Bani Isra'il.

easy.set: Five small creatures named in the Qur'an
easy.explain: The Qur'an mentions the bee, the ant, the spider, the fly and the gnat. Three surahs are named after the first three.

easy.set: Five fruits named in the Qur'an
easy.explain: The Qur'an names the date palm, grapes, pomegranates, olives and figs.

easy.set: Five colours named in the Qur'an
easy.explain: Surah Fatir mentions white, red and black streaks in the mountains, Al-Kahf green garments, and Al-Baqarah the yellow cow.

easy.set: The four rivers of Paradise in Surah Muhammad
items: Water that does not go stale
Wine delicious to those who drink
easy.explain: Surah Muhammad describes rivers of unchanging water, milk, delicious wine and pure honey.
Surah Al-Kahf tells four stories: the sleepers in the cave, the man with two gardens, Musa and the servant of Allah, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

medium.set: Prophets named together in Al-Anbiya 21:85
medium.explain: Allah says, "And Isma'il and Idris and Dhul-Kifl, all were among the patient."

medium.set: Prophets named in Surah Sad 38:45 to 48
medium.explain: Surah Sad tells the Prophet ﷺ to remember Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub, and Isma'il, Al-Yasa' and Dhul-Kifl.

medium.set: Names of Allah in Al-Hashr 59:23
medium.explain: Al-Hashr 23 names Allah the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Giver of security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller and the Supreme.

medium.set: Names of Allah in Al-Hashr 59:24
medium.explain: Al-Hashr 24: He is Allah, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. His are the best names, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

medium.set: Names of Allah in Al-Hadid 57:3
medium.explain: Al-Hadid 3: He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward.

medium.set: Names of Allah in Ayat al-Kursi
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi calls Allah the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, the Most High, the Most Great.

medium.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah Al-Fajr
medium.explain: Surah Al-Fajr opens: "By the dawn, and the ten nights, and the even and the odd, and the night when it departs."

medium.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah At-Tur
medium.explain: Surah At-Tur swears by the Mount, a Book inscribed, the much-frequented House, the raised roof and the kindled sea.

medium.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah Al-Buruj
medium.explain: Surah Al-Buruj swears by the sky with its great stars, the promised Day, and the witness and what is witnessed.

medium.set: What Allah swears by at the start of Surah Al-Layl
items: The creation of male and female
medium.explain: Surah Al-Layl swears by the night as it covers, the day as it shines, and the creation of male and female.

medium.set: The signs sent on Fir'awn's people in Surah Al-A'raf 7:133
medium.explain: Allah sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as clear signs.

medium.set: Luqman's advice to his son
items: Do not associate partners with Allah
Be patient with what befalls you
Do not turn your cheek in pride
decoys: Gather as much wealth as you can
medium.explain: Surah Luqman gives his advice: no shirk, prayer, enjoining good, patience, humility, moderation in walking and lowering the voice.

medium.set: What is made attractive to people in Ali 'Imran 3:14
medium.explain: Ali 'Imran 14 lists what is made beautiful to people of worldly desires, then says that with Allah is the better return.

medium.set: Animals for riding and beauty in An-Nahl 16:8
medium.explain: An-Nahl 8: "And horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride, and as adornment."

medium.set: Five foods forbidden in Al-Ma'idah 5:3
medium.explain: Al-Ma'idah 3 forbids carrion, blood, swine, what is dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled, the beaten, the fallen and the gored, among others.

medium.set: Seven of the relatives one may never marry, from An-Nisa 4:23
medium.explain: An-Nisa 23 lists them. Cousins are not among those forbidden.

medium.set: Qualities of the successful believers in Al-Mu'minun
items: They are humble in their prayers
They turn away from idle talk
They keep their trusts and promises
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mu'minun opens by describing the successful believers in these terms.

medium.set: Five qualities of the servants of the Most Merciful in Al-Furqan
items: They walk humbly on the earth
They spend the night in prostration
They do not call on another god
They do not bear false witness
decoys: They speak harshly to the ignorant
medium.explain: The end of Al-Furqan describes the servants of the Most Merciful.

medium.set: The seven destructive sins
items: Killing a soul Allah has forbidden
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Avoid the seven destructive sins," and named these.

medium.set: Five creatures that may be killed even in the Haram
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said five harmful creatures may be killed even in the sanctuary.

medium.set: The major signs of the Hour in Sahih Muslim
items: The sun rising from the west
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until ten signs appear, and named these.

medium.set: What the Prophet ﷺ sought refuge from after the final tashahhud
items: The trials of life and death
medium.explain: He taught us to seek refuge from four: the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the Dajjal.

medium.set: The three who stayed behind from Tabuk
medium.explain: Ka'b named the two others who stayed behind with him: Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah.

medium.set: The sons of the Prophet ﷺ
medium.explain: According to most historians the Prophet's sons were al-Qasim and Abdullah, born to Khadijah, and Ibrahim, born to Mariyah. All three died young.

medium.set: Angels named in the Prophet's night prayer supplication
medium.explain: He opened his night prayer with, "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil."

medium.set: Women given as examples in Surah At-Tahrim
medium.explain: At-Tahrim gives the wives of Nuh and Lut as examples for the disbelievers, and Fir'awn's wife and Maryam for the believers.

medium.set: The five things only Allah knows, in Surah Luqman 31:34
items: What a soul will earn tomorrow
In what land a soul will die
medium.explain: Luqman 34 lists them, and the Prophet ﷺ called them the five keys of the unseen.

medium.set: Metals named in the Qur'an
medium.explain: Al-Hadid names iron, Al-Kahf molten copper, and gold and silver appear in several verses.

medium.set: What rain brings forth in An-Nahl 16:11
medium.explain: An-Nahl 11: with it He grows for you crops, olives, date palms, grapes and every kind of fruit.

medium.set: Righteousness in Ayat al-Birr (Al-Baqarah 2:177)
items: Giving wealth to relatives and orphans
decoys: Turning to the east or the west
medium.explain: Al-Baqarah 177 says righteousness is not turning your faces east or west, but belief, giving, prayer, zakat, keeping promises and patience.

medium.set: Prophets whose stories are told in Surah Hud
medium.explain: Surah Hud tells of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb, and mentions Musa.

medium.set: Prophets whose stories are told in Surah Ash-Shu'ara
medium.explain: Ash-Shu'ara tells the stories of Musa, Ibrahim, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, each ending with the same refrain.

hard.set: The seven famous reciters of the Qur'an
hard.explain: These seven reciters, chosen by Ibn Mujahid, are the basis of the seven readings. Hafs and Warsh are narrators from two of them.
Surah Maryam names Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa, Ibrahim, Musa, Harun, Isma'il and Idris.
An-Nisa 163 lists those to whom Allah gave revelation as He gave it to the Prophet ﷺ.

hard.set: Those Allah chose above the worlds in Ali 'Imran 3:33
hard.explain: Ali 'Imran 33: Allah chose Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran above the worlds.

hard.set: The kinds of tawaf in Hajj
hard.explain: The tawaf of arrival, the tawaf of ifadah after Arafah, and the farewell tawaf before leaving.
'Abasa lists grain, grapes, herbage, olives, date palms, gardens, fruit and fodder.

items: Do not kill your children for fear of poverty
Do not walk on the earth arrogantly
hard.explain: Al-Isra 23 to 37 gathers these commands, from tawhid and kindness to parents to honest measure and humility.

hard.set: Kings the Prophet ﷺ wrote to
hard.explain: After Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ sent letters inviting rulers to Islam, among them these four.

hard.set: The three idols named in Surah An-Najm
hard.explain: An-Najm 19 and 20: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?"
Surah Nuh 23 names the five idols his people refused to abandon.
